description.value: A cross-sectional fMRI study examined relationships between fasting acylated ghrelin and BOLD activity during viewing of high- and low-calorie food cues in women with active anorexia nervosa, weight-recovered anorexia nervosa, and healthy-weight controls.

value: We hypothesized that healthy-weight control women would demonstrate significant relationships between acylated ghrelin and BOLD activity in homeostatic (hypothalamus) and hedonic (nucleus accumbens, amygdala, hippocampus, insula, and OFC) circuitry in response to food stimuli in a fasting state, and further that the direction of these relationships would vary across stimuli of different hedonic value: positive associations for high-calorie foods and negative relationships in response to low-calorie foods.
we additionally hypothesized that this pattern of associations would be disrupted in women with active AN and AN-WR.

description.value: Cross-sectional study of active anorexia nervosa, weight-recovered anorexia nervosa, and healthy-weight control women.

name.value: High-calorie foods vs. objects: positive relationship in HC

definition.value: Relationship between fasting plasma acylated ghrelin and ROI activity in response to high-calorie foods versus objects in healthy-weight control women.

value: Fasting acylated ghrelin was positively associated with BOLD activation to high-calorie foods versus objects in the right amygdala, hippocampus, anterior insula, and orbitofrontal cortex in healthy-weight control women.

These findings provide evidence of the hedonic role of ghrelin in human appetite and suggest coordinated biasing toward intake of high-calorie food through ghrelin action on these regions during fasting.

spans.text: _a Coordinates are presented in MNI space._

name.value: Low-calorie foods vs. objects: positive relationship in AN

definition.value: Relationship between fasting plasma acylated ghrelin and ROI activity in response to low-calorie foods versus objects in women with AN.

value: Regression of acylated ghrelin on activation in response to low-calorie foods versus objects yielded a positive association in the right orbitofrontal cortex in the AN group.
The positive association may reflect the tight coupling between ghrelin and the reversed hedonic coding of low-calorie foods as highly rewarding in active anorexia nervosa.

spans.text: _a Coordinates are presented in MNI space._

name.value: High-calorie foods vs. objects: negative relationship in AN-WR

definition.value: Negative relationship between fasting plasma acylated ghrelin and BOLD activation to high-calorie foods versus objects in women with AN-WR.

value: Women with AN-WR exhibited a significant negative relationship between acylated ghrelin levels and BOLD activation to high-calorie foods versus objects in the left hippocampus.

The opposing direction of ghrelin and activity in the left hippocampus in women with AN-WR may indicate persistence of abnormal ghrelin signaling after weight recovery and perhaps serve as a biomarker for vulnerability to relapse.
